q_before.title: The Days Before
q_before.summary: Three years an apprentice and lately old enough to be asked what happens next. There is work, and there are people, and there is a stranger on the green.
q_before.dm_notes: THE PROLOGUE IS THE POINT. Do not hurry the player toward a plot. Let them be eighteen in a village that likes them: Cotter in the forge, Nell in the bakehouse, Jory everywhere, Bryn underfoot. Vosk is on the green asking polite questions in a particular order — about the hall, about the smith, about who came to Wickmoor when. He is never threatening. He is always slightly too interested. The burning comes when the player leaves for the river; until then, give them the life they are about to lose, and make it worth losing.

steps.desc: Spend the days: the forge, the green, whoever you want to see

leads.text: Cotter has been short with you all week, and he is never short with you.
The traveller on the green keeps asking about the moot hall.
Jory wants to fish the bend before the weather turns. He has asked four times.

q_the_burning.title: The Smoke Over Wickmoor
q_the_burning.summary: Smoke over the valley, and four of you an hour's run away.
q_the_burning.dm_notes: They are at the river when Sibby sees it — she always sees it first. Do not describe the raiders; they are gone before the party arrives. Describe the walk back and what is in it. Half the village. The forge still standing, which is worse. Halla and Dunn are dead. BRYN IS NOT AMONG THE DEAD AND IS NOT ANYWHERE. Ilsa Rooke is alive for as long as the scene needs her and no longer. The raiders wore no colours and their boots were new and matched.

on_complete.text: Half of Wickmoor burned while four of us were at the river.
The raiders wore no colours, and their boots were new and all the same.
Bryn is not among the dead, and she is not anywhere.

leads.text: Sibby says the smoke is coming off the green, not the fields. That means houses.
Tam went straight up the bank without waiting. He is already half a mile ahead.
The high wood looks down on the whole valley. From up there you would see what is left.

q_the_road.title: What Ilsa Rooke Said
q_the_road.summary: Go to Harrowmoot. Not for help — for the other thing.
q_the_road.dm_notes: Ilsa dies giving this. She is not gentle about it and she does not explain, because she has spent eleven years deciding people were not ready and she knows, now, that she was wrong and there is no time to be right. WHAT SHE ACTUALLY SAYS: go to Harrowmoot, find the one who took the other half of the keeping, and tell them Wickmoor is finished. She will name no name — she gets as far as 'ask at the' and stops. If pressed for what was kept, she looks at JORY, not at the player, and that is all. Her last instruction is a warning: once you ask, none of you go back to being who you were this morning. Let the player hear it as grief. It is not grief.

steps.desc: Take the north road to Harrowmoot

leads.text: Harrowmoot is two days north at a walk, and it is the only place near enough to matter.
Cotter will not come with you. He will not say why, and he has already packed your bag.
Hob says the tithe-collector's gig went north an hour before the smoke.

q_the_keeping.title: The Other Half of the Keeping
q_the_keeping.summary: Ilsa Rooke said to find the one who took the other half. She did not finish saying where, and she is not going to.
q_the_keeping.dm_notes:
THE ANSWER IS SAVERI CROLE, and she assays lamp-oil contracts on Assay Row. She was Accord. She hid the other half of what Wickmoor kept, and then she took a job with the people looking for it, because the safest place to stand is behind them. She has been nobody for eleven years and it has cost her every single day.

THREE WAYS TO HER, and the players will find at most two:
  1. EMERIC SALLOW in the Pensioners' Hall remembers every certificate the Arcanate      ever issued, including one to a woman who stopped collecting her pension the same      month the Accord lost the war. He will trade the name — not for money, which he      refuses, but for being owed something by somebody. Let him name the terms.
  2. BEL in the Cut knows there is a Shepherd in the Row and hates her for it. She will      give the name gladly and for the wrong reasons, and what she wants in exchange is      help burning the assay ledger.
  3. RUE TAMSIN will not tell anyone anything. But Saveri drinks at the Fetterlock every      eighth day, alone, and Rue seats her where the door is visible. A player who watches      the room rather than asking questions can simply see it.

WHEN THEY REACH HER SHE SAYS NO. Not evasively — she tells them the truth and then refuses. What she kept was never an object and it was never hers to give back. She believes, with reason, that the moment she says the rest of it out loud the boy is finished. She is not protecting a secret. She is protecting Jory, and she is wrong, and she has been wrong in exactly this way for eleven years.

DO NOT LET HER BE PERSUADED BY A GOOD ROLL. This is the sealed kind. What moves her is one of: Vosk getting close enough that hiding stops working, Jory's pact waking where she can see it, or somebody telling her what happened to Bryn Wick.

on_complete.text: Saveri Crole assays contracts on the Row, and she was Accord before that.
Saveri Crole. Assay Row, and she does not leave it.

steps.desc: Ask her for the other half

on_complete.text: Saveri Crole says what Wickmoor kept was never an object, and refuses to say more.
She is not hiding it from you. She is hiding it from Jory.

leads.text: Ilsa said 'ask at the' and did not finish. Harrowmoot has three places worth asking.
The Pensioners' Hall keeps every Arcanate certificate ever issued, and a man who remembers them.
There is somebody in the Cut who hates whoever it is you are looking for.
Rue Tamsin seats one particular customer where she can see the door.

q_the_ledger.title: What the Row Keeps
q_the_ledger.summary: Somewhere under Assay Row there is a book with the name of every unlicensed caster in forty miles in it. Bel wants it burnt. Barthel Onn wants it never mentioned again. You have not decided what you want.
q_the_ledger.dm_notes:
THE LEDGER IS REAL and it is in the undercroft, third press, closed-year stamp 1184. It lists ninety-one names, of which eleven are dead and two are children. One of the children is Jory Finch, entered under a name that is not his.

FOUR WAYS IN, and each costs something different:
  1. BARTHEL ONN has a key and no spine. He will not hand it over — but his wife MARDA      does the Row's real filing, is furious about the spring audit, and will trade the      press number for a promise to get Barthel out before the next one.
  2. TEAL, the Cut runner, will lift the key for a price she names herself. She will      also be caught, eventually, if you let her.
  3. FERRIN OAKE at the Bonding House can requisition a ledger legitimately. He will do      it to look useful to somebody senior, and will absolutely mention it afterwards.
  4. Through the cistern. Wet, cold, and nobody is watching it, because nobody has      fitted in thirty years.

WHAT THEY DO WITH IT IS THE POINT. Burning it protects ninety-one people and destroys the only proof of what the Syndicate has been collecting. Copying it protects the proof and leaves the names where they are. Handing it to Saltbeck is a real option and the worst one, and he will pay.

DO NOT RESOLVE THIS FOR THEM. If they ask what the right thing is, the honest answer from every character in this town is a different one.

steps.desc: Find out what the Row keeps under it
Decide what the names are worth

leads.text: Bel says there is a book under the Row with her brother's name in it.

q_the_pension.title: Four Marks a Month
q_the_pension.summary: Emeric Sallow's Arcanate pension is four marks a month. Emeric Sallow has not been paid in six years. Somebody is still collecting it.
q_the_pension.dm_notes:
THE ANSWER IS UNCOMFORTABLE: the pension is being drawn by the Pensioners' Hall itself, against Emeric's name, and it is what feeds MOSS and the other three survivors. The clerk who set it up died four years ago. Nobody currently alive decided to do this; everybody currently alive is living on it.

EMERIC KNOWS. That is the part that lands. He has known for two years and has said nothing, because the alternative is four old people with nothing, and because being owed something is the last thing he has that is worth anything.

THIS IS A SIDE QUEST AND IT SHOULD FEEL LIKE ONE — small, quiet, and finishable in an afternoon. Its real function is that solving it kindly is what makes EMERIC name Saveri Crole without being asked. He does not trade information for money. He trades it for being owed something by somebody who turned out to be worth owing.

IF THEY EXPOSE IT instead: the Hall loses the pension, Moss loses the cohort list they have been keeping for thirty years, and Emeric answers nothing, ever again.

steps.desc: Find out who is drawing Emeric's pension
Settle it, one way or the other

leads.text: Emeric Sallow says his pension was four marks a month. He says it as if it still is.

q_the_fetterlock.title: Who They Took Instead
q_the_fetterlock.summary: Calder Wick has walked to Harrowmoot every week since the fire, asking after a nine-year-old girl. The Fetterlock holds people against debts. Rue Tamsin will not discuss her guests.
q_the_fetterlock.dm_notes:
BRYN WICK IS NOT IN THE FETTERLOCK. She was, for eleven days, under a debt that was not hers, and then she was moved — because somebody realised she was the wrong child and that the right one was still in Wickmoor. That somebody is the same somebody who burnt it.

WHAT IS IN THE FETTERLOCK is the intake book, and HASK the day warder who would genuinely rather not write an incident report about anything at all. He can be talked past, bored past, drunk past, or simply walked past on the eighth day. Rue will not help and will not stop them; she is not a jailer, she is a landlord with a bad contract.

THE ENTRY READS: 'W., f., 9, against Wickmoor tithe arrears. Released to contract.' Released to contract is not a thing that happens to children. It is the phrase the Row uses when a person becomes part of a bond.

THIS IS WHERE VOSK STOPS BEING A MYSTERY AND BECOMES A PROBLEM. The contract number in the intake book is the one Vosk is here to close.

IF THEY TELL CALDER: he goes to the Counting House and asks Saltbeck directly, which is brave and stupid, and he does not come back out the same. Let them stop him if they move fast. Do not stop him for them.

steps.desc: Find out whether Bryn was ever here
Find out what 'released to contract' means

leads.text: Calder Wick is at the tollgate again, asking after a nine-year-old girl.

q_what_cotter_did.title: The Last Year of the War
q_what_cotter_did.summary: Cotter Vane has been short with you for a week, and he has never been short with you. Something he did eleven years ago is walking up the north road with a contract in its hand.
q_what_cotter_did.dm_notes:
COTTER CARRIED THE KEEPING. That is the whole of it. In the last year of the war an Accord courier put two things into Wickmoor for safekeeping: a child, and the binding that made the child what he is. Cotter took the child to the Finches and told nobody, including his own apprentice, for eleven years.

HE IS NOT ASHAMED OF HIDING IT. He is ashamed that he was glad — that when the courier died on the moor he felt relief, because it meant nobody would come back for the boy and he could keep pretending the forge was the whole world.

HE WILL NOT SAY THIS UNPROMPTED. Trust is what opens it, and only trust: he has been asked before, by people with better arguments than any roll will produce. What moves him is the player having already done something he would have done.

IF COTTER IS DEAD when this opens, ILSA ROOKE carries it instead and says it worse — she was Accord, she knows what the binding was for, and she has been angry at him about it for eleven years. That is not a different quest. It is the same thing said by somebody with less love in it, which is how a world that has moved on is supposed to feel.

leads.text: Cotter has been short with you all week, and he is never short with you.

q_the_contract.title: The Contract Closes
q_the_contract.summary: Amery Vosk came to Wickmoor to close a contract. The contract is not for oil, and it is not for land, and the clock on it is nearly out.
q_the_contract.dm_notes:
THE CONTRACT IS FOR A PERSON. Bond 1184/7, held by the Meridian Syndicate against the Wickmoor lamp-tithe, secured on 'the keeping' — a phrase the Row uses without ever asking what is inside it. Vosk has spent four days trying to close it politely, because he believes that is possible. SALTBECK does not, and Saltbeck has been sent to do it the other way.

VOSK IS NOT THE VILLAIN AND SHOULD NOT PLAY AS ONE. He is a competent man with a signed instruction who has worked out, somewhere around day three, what he is actually collecting. He has not told Aurelane. He is looking for a reason to fail, and he will not invent one — somebody has to hand it to him.

THREE ENDINGS, all of them legitimate, none of them clean:
  VOID IT.    The ledger, the intake book and Emeric's pension together prove the tithe was               collected twice. A bond secured on a debt that was already paid is void. This               takes paperwork, not a sword, and it requires the players to have been thorough               rather than brave.
  BUY IT.     Saveri Crole can close the bond by naming herself as the keeping. She has been               waiting eleven years for somebody to give her a reason, and it costs her               everything. DO NOT let the players engineer this without her choosing it.
  BREAK IT.   Take the strongroom. It works, it is loud, and the Syndicate does not forget a               broken door — every price in Harrowmoot goes up within the month and the players               will hear about it from people they like.

IF JORY IS DEAD: the bond is secured on a keeping that no longer exists, which does not void it — it makes it TRANSFERABLE. Saltbeck's instruction says 'the keeping', not a name, and Bryn Wick is nine and was already taken once by people who had the wrong child. The war still comes; it just comes for somebody else. Do not soften this and do not stage a rescue the players did not earn.

steps.desc: Find out what Vosk is actually here to collect

leads.text: The traveller on the green keeps asking about the moot hall.
